references.text: Job 39:30 describes how eagle chicks drink blood, and 'where the slain are, there it is.' This is a direct parallel image to Jesus' words that where the body is, there the vultures will gather. [ref:Job 39:30|Job 39:30]

Habakkuk 1:8 describes the Chaldeans' horses as flying 'like an eagle swooping down on its prey,' an image of swift judgment and destruction that is also present in Jesus' imagery. [ref:Hab 1:8|Habakkuk 1:8]

Matthew 24:28 is the direct parallel to this verse: 'For where the carcass is, there the vultures will gather.' Jesus uses the same proverb in his eschatological discourse. [ref:Matt 24:28|Matthew 24:28]

Ezekiel 39:17 contains God's call to the birds to gather for a great sacrificial feast, where they are to eat flesh and drink blood. The image of birds gathering over dead bodies parallels Jesus' imagery concerning judgment. [ref:Ezek 39:17|Ezekiel 39:17]

In Deuteronomy 28:49 God's judgment is described as a people coming 'like an eagle flies,' an image of inevitable and sudden judgment, which is the theme in Jesus' words. [ref:Deut 28:49|Deuteronomy 28:49]

The preceding verses in Luke 17:34–36 describe the sudden separation between people at the judgment—two on one bed, two grinding grain—and the disciples' question 'Where, Lord?' in verse 37 is a response to this. [ref:Luke 17:34-36|Luke 17:34-36]

Revelation 19:17–18 depicts an angel calling all the birds to 'the great supper of God' to eat flesh from kings and mighty ones—an eschatological image of judgment that reflects Jesus' proverb about vultures gathering over the body. [ref:Rev 19:17-18|Revelation 19:17–18]

Isaiah 46:11 speaks of God calling a bird of prey from the east, the one who will fulfill his plan. The eagle/bird of prey as God's instrument in judgment is a recurring biblical motif underlying Jesus' imagery. [ref:Isa 46:11|Isaiah 46:11]
